corrections.issue: Timing sequence garbled: he did not move from Q4 2023 to end-2023. He first expected the downturn in Q4 2023, pulled it forward to 'now' after SVB on anecdotal leading data (trucks, retail), and now thinks that was wrong and is going back to end-2023, while saying he does not know. The shift to worrying more about growth than inflation dates from the previous September.
corrections.fix: Since the previous September he worries more about growth than inflation; he first dated the downturn to Q4 2023, pulled it forward after SVB on anecdotal leading data (trucks, retail), and now moves it back to end-2023, admitting he does not really know.

corrections.issue: Direction of the argument inverted: he does not say a 10-month run is 'not unusual'; he says real secular moves do not last only 10 months, so if AI is real the Nvidia move has further to run despite short-term drawdown risk.
corrections.fix: Real secular technology moves last years (dot-com 2-2.5 years, about 4 for Cisco and Sun), so if AI is real Nvidia's 10-month rise from about 100 to 380 should not be the end; it could fall materially short term, but he expects to hold it at least two or three years.

completeness_estimate: 0.86 - first reader caught all major fiscal, liquidity, credit, AI and shorting ideas; missed a few secondary points (AI winner dispersion, hidden fragility from no bankruptcies, narrow US breadth, index-short losses, forecast-adjustment process).
